solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Call up from inmate's cell, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase before it is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: an inmate is a con, and a cell can be a crypt (an underground chamber), giving con's crypt

explanation.surface: A prisoner's cell sounds out a call to arms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' tells you that CON'S CRYPT, said aloud, gives the spelling of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To conscript someone is to draft them into military service, the same as calling them up.

indicators.note: losing head means the word must drop its first letter

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship, and left's is read as left is, giving ports

explanation.surface: What is left of someone who has lost their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' takes the first letter P off PORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Orts are scraps of leftover food, an old word for remains.

clue.text: Cork by end of knots on hat

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means this piece sits above the next one
end of means only the final letter of knots is taken

parts.note: a topper is a top hat

explanation.surface: Someone ties knots near a cork attached to a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'on' puts the S from 'end of knots' above TOPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cork is a type of stopper that seals a bottle neck.

indicators.note: after places the piece for responsibility behind the piece for crash

parts.note: to ram is to crash into something
one's part is one's share of a duty, a responsibility

explanation.surface: A bank takes the blame after a financial crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial, but here it is an earth bank; 'after' sets the responsibility behind the crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is a defensive wall or embankment of earth, so it is a bank.

clue.text: Starts to put on sexy exhibition?

definitions.text: Starts to put on sexy exhibition?

indicators.note: Starts to tells you to take the first letter of each word after it

explanation.surface: Someone begins a racy display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts to' picks the first letters of put, on, sexy and exhibition. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking a pose for a sexy display is a way of showing yourself off, as the whole clue says.

clue.text: Throttling, twisting gag in last turn

indicators.note: twisting tells you to rearrange the letters of the words after it

explanation.surface: A struggle with a gag ends in someone being choked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisting' rearranges GAG IN LAST TURN.
explanation.definitionFit: Strangulating means choking or squeezing the throat, which is throttling.

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions to tie up a steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like an order to tie up the ship. 'possibly' rearranges MOOR STEAMSHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A metamorphosis is a complete change of form, a thorough alteration.

parts.note: reads like Wellington commanding at the battle, but Waterloo is also a big London railway terminus with its own official in charge

explanation.surface: Who was the commander at the Battle of Waterloo?
explanation.walkthrough: Waterloo suggests the 1815 battle; it is also a major London railway terminus.
explanation.definitionFit: A stationmaster is the official who runs a railway station such as London Waterloo.

clue.text: So, to free her, let loose

indicators.note: let loose says the letters are set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to release a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let loose' rearranges TO FREE HER.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and so are synonyms, both meaning for that reason.

indicators.note: in places the piece for Tries inside the piece for physical

parts.note: physical things are real, tangible
a judge tries a case, that is, hears it

explanation.surface: Rugby tries scored during a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tries' suggests rugby, and 'physical exercise' looks like one phrase; split it, and 'in' puts the hearing inside the physical.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice run, an exercise before the real performance.

parts.note: the man is he, with the 's read as is linking to what follows
D is the usual abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: Someone notes the US president belongs to the Democratic party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President' suggests the White House, but here it is a chairperson or head of a body.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of an organisation such as a college or society.

indicators.note: dropping says a letter must be taken out of the word for plea

parts.note: an appeal is a plea or earnest request
E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A request that has given up a drug comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes E out of APPEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal someone is to fill them with horror, to shock them.

parts.note: an overweight person is fat
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter, E

explanation.surface: A romance finishing with a portly lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' looks like a lover; it is the heart, the centre letter, of 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fate can mean one's end or death, as in meeting one's fate.

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gable suits a chilly bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gable' looks like part of a roof, but it is Clark Gable, the Hollywood star.
explanation.definitionFit: Clark Gable was a famous film actor, so Gable is an example of someone with this first name.

clue.text: Trims top off rows of bushes

indicators.note: top off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: hedges are rows of bushes

explanation.surface: A gardener cuts the tops off the hedges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top off' removes H from HEDGES.
explanation.definitionFit: Edges are borders or trims along the side of something.

explanation.surface: A career soldier who has become a general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like a rank; here it means ordinary or usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a soldier in the permanent army, and regular also means general, normal or usual.

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
a pole is a rod or staff

explanation.surface: Someone with a small fishing rod catching a shrimp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrimp' is a small person or thing; a tadpole is a small young frog, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimp is slang for a tiny creature, and a tadpole is a tiny young frog, a shrimp of sorts.

indicators.note: of says the answer is made from the letters of the words after it, here sitting inside them

explanation.surface: The support of the faithful is falling away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' points into 'faithful crumbling', which holds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fulcrum is the pivot on which a lever turns, its support.

clue.text: Ovation ends in procession for Queen

indicators.note: in places the pair of letters inside the piece for procession

parts.note: a march is a procession

indicators.note: ends picks the first and last letters of Ovation

explanation.surface: Applause rings out as the Queen passes in a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends' gives O and N, the first and last letters of Ovation, and 'in' puts them inside MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A queen who reigns is a monarch, a sovereign ruler.

explanation.surface: A secret agent is on board a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' looks like a verb; it is a sleeping-car train.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeper is an overnight train with berths, and also a spy who lies dormant until called into action.

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Marines gather on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges MARINES.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a meeting for discussion or training.

indicators.note: appears before puts the piece for Snitch in front of the next piece

parts.note: to rat is to inform on someone, to snitch

explanation.surface: An informer stands in court before an English judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'judge' is a verb here, and 'appears before' looks like court language; it just sets RAT in front of E.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to assess or judge its value.

clue.text: Garden's naff ornament mocked endlessly, initially

definitions.text: Garden's naff ornament mocked endlessly, initially

indicators.note: initially says to take the first letter of each word before it

explanation.surface: A tacky garden ornament has long been derided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' picks the first letters of Garden's naff ornament mocked endlessly, and the clue as a whole describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden gnome is the classic kitsch ornament, endlessly mocked as naff, which is British slang for tacky.

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A French firm has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cola is a fizzy soft drink.

indicators.note: following puts the game after the abbreviation for the Commission

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union, a game

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's game is played after the European Commission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' suggests the UK prime minister Gordon Brown; it is a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is a pale greyish-brown or beige colour, a shade of brown.

indicators.note: ignoring says a letter is left out of the word for Labour's

parts.note: labours are tasks, read here as plural

indicators.note: leader picks the first letter of Tory

explanation.surface: Labour questions why the Tory leader is being ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party; it is work. 'ignoring' drops T, from 'Tory leader', from TASKS.
explanation.definitionFit: Questions as a verb means asks, as in she questions him.

clue.text: Isn't archaic? No, becoming out of date

indicators.note: becoming says these letters turn into something new when rearranged

explanation.surface: A protest that something is not old-fashioned, met with a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' rearranges ISN'T ARCHAIC NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Anachronistic means belonging to another period, old-fashioned and out of date.

indicators.note: taking means the piece for choice takes in the following letters

parts.note: best means the choicest, the pick
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, posh
a daily is a British cleaner who comes in by day; another name is char

explanation.surface: The best capital is reached via a posh daily newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' suggests a newspaper, but a daily is a British term for a cleaning woman; 'taking' puts posh and daily inside choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucharest is the capital city of Romania.
